text: Given no X-DigitalOcean-Api-Key header is sent, When any tool is called over POST /mcp, Then the server returns HTTP 401 naming the required header, and zero outbound calls are made to api.digitalocean.com
steps: Start the service locally (docker-compose up or uv run python -m digitalocean_databases_mcp)
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
Inspect the mocked/real outbound HTTP client call count for the duration of the request
expect: Response status 401; body text mentions X-DigitalOcean-Api-Key; outbound call count to api.digitalocean.com is 0

text: Given a valid token, When do_list_clusters is called, Then every returned item has id/name/engine/status/region and none contains a password-shaped field
Given cluster_id belonging to token A, When do_get_cluster is called with token B, Then the tool returns not_found rather than token A's cluster data
Given the DigitalOcean API mock returns 429 with Retry-After, When a tool calls it, Then the client backs off and retries, and a still-429 result maps to error.code=rate_limited with retryable=true
Given a cluster_id that does not exist, When a cluster-scoped tool is called, Then the result is {"error":{"code":"not_found",...}} and not an unhandled exception or 500
Given required fields (name, engine, region, size), When do_create_cluster is called against a mocked 201, Then the tool result has status creating
do_destroy_cluster's declared tool schema has exactly one required parameter (cluster_id, string) and no tag/filter/bulk parameter
do_update_firewall_rules's tool description explicitly states it replaces the entire trusted-sources list; calling it with a 1-item list after existing rules leaves exactly 1 rule, not a union
Given two concurrent requests with two different bearer tokens, When each calls a tool at the same time, Then each response reflects only its own token's mocked data, with no cross-request leakage

Given a mocked 75-item cluster list and no explicit limit, When do_list_clusters is called, Then the result has at most 50 items and has_more=true; given limit=500, the effective per_page sent upstream is clamped to 200

Given a real DigitalOcean account with at least one cluster, When tools/list then tools/call do_list_clusters is run over HTTP with a real token, Then the response lists that account's actual cluster(s)
steps: Obtain a real DigitalOcean personal access token from a test/trial account (Control Panel -> Account -> API -> Tokens)
expect: 200 response whose body lists the account's real clusters (or an empty array if the account has none) -- not an error
evidence: needs a real DigitalOcean vendor account; not available at design time. Does not block merge/registration/INT publish per SOP.

text: Given a real DigitalOcean account, When do_create_cluster (smallest size) is called then do_destroy_cluster on the same id, Then both round-trip successfully against the live API
steps: Using a real token, call do_create_cluster with the smallest available size/region from do_list_cluster_options
Poll do_get_cluster until status is online (or accept status creating as sufficient evidence the call was accepted)
Call do_destroy_cluster with the returned cluster id
Call do_get_cluster again and confirm not_found
expect: Cluster is created (visible via do_get_cluster) and then destroyed (subsequent do_get_cluster returns not_found)
evidence: needs a real DigitalOcean vendor account; creating/destroying a real cluster also has a billing implication, so this is explicitly deferred to whoever owns a funded test account. Does not block merge/registration/INT publish.

text: A raw curl tools/list request without the credential header is rejected by the running Starlette middleware itself (not just a unit-test mock)
steps: curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'

text: A raw curl tools/list request WITH a credential header succeeds with 200, not 400, confirming stateless_http=True is actually wired
steps: curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'X-DigitalOcean-Api-Key: placeholder-token' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
expect: HTTP/1.1 200 response (not 400), per the SOP 1.3 self-check for stateless_http
